spec.claim_summary: A monthly rule buys bitcoin on the last day of the month when price is above the 200-day SMA and sells when price is below it.
assumptions: BTC-USD mapped to Binance spot symbol BTCUSDT.
Timeframe set to 1d because the rule uses a 200-day SMA and last-day-of-month calendar logic; no explicit bar timeframe is stated.
Price interpreted as daily close for both the 200-day SMA comparison and the above/below checks.
Direction is long-only; selling interpreted as exiting to flat, not opening a short position.
Entry requires both conditions on the same bar close: last day of month and close above 200-day SMA.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: the claim requires the sell check only on the last day of the month, i.e. close below 200-day SMA AND last day of month on the same bar, but the schema evaluates exit conditions as OR (ANY true exits) so an AND exit cannot be enforced exactly; both legs are included as exit[0] and exit[1] to document intent.
No stop, target, trailing stop or max hold stated, so position is held until the exit signal.

evidence.quote: buying when the price is above the 200-day simple moving average (SMA)
on the last day of the month
on the last day of the month

audit_majors: exit: Claim requires sell only when close is below 200-day SMA ON the last day of month (AND). Spec encodes them as two separate exit legs which evaluate as OR: exit[0] fires on any bar below SMA without month filter, and exit[1] fires on every last-day-of-month even when above SMA. This invents unconditional monthly exits and intra-month exits.
